Change c0062. Location: 1818 Vol. I, Ch. II; 1831 Ch. III.

Context before (unchanged): These are the reflections of the first days; but when the lapse of time proves the reality of the evil, then the actual bitterness of grief commences.

1818 text: Yet from whom has not that rude hand rent away some dear connexion; and why should I describe a sorrow which all have felt, and must feel?

1831 text: Yet from whom has not that rude hand rent away some dear connection? and why should I describe a sorrow which all have felt, and must feel?

Diff: Yet from whom has not that rude hand rent away some dear [-connexion;-] {+connection?+} and why should I describe a sorrow which all have felt, and must feel?

Context after (unchanged): The time at length arrives, when grief is rather an indulgence than a necessity; and the smile that plays upon the lips, although it may be deemed a sacrilege, is not banished.

result.rationale: 'connexion' becomes 'connection' (orthographic modernization), but the semicolon becomes a question mark, turning the rhetorical clause into a question. Mainly spelling, with a punctuation-driven shift in syntax.
